html:
Enlhet-Enenlhet is the name of a family of related languages and peoples of the Paraguayan Chaco, among them the Enlhet, Enxet, Sanapaná, Angaité and Toba-Maskoy. They lived as hunters, gatherers and small farmers in the dry thorn forest and palm savannas west of the Paraguay River.

From the 1880s land companies and ranchers bought up the Chaco. From 1927 German-speaking Mennonite colonists settled in the heart of Enlhet land, and the Chaco War between Paraguay and Bolivia (1932 to 1935) was fought across the region. Many Enlhet became workers on Mennonite farms. Several Enxet communities have since won land cases at the Inter-American Court of Human Rights.
